items.new: But here it must be noted that owing to the relentless activity with which sperm whales have lately been hunted over all four oceans, they now frequently gather in extensive herds, instead of almost invariably sailing in small, separate groups as in former times. Sometimes these herds embrace so great a multitude that it would almost seem as if numerous nations of them had sworn a solemn league and covenant for mutual assistance and protection. To this gathering of sperm whales into such immense caravans may be attributed the fact that even in the best cruising grounds, you may now sometimes sail for weeks and months without being greeted by a single spout — and then be suddenly confronted by what sometimes seems thousands upon thousands.

items.new: Now, including the occasional wide intervals between the revolving outer circles and the spaces between the various pods in any one of those circles, the entire area taken up by the whole multitude at this point must have contained at least two or three square miles. At any rate — though such a measurement at such a time might be deceptive — spouts could be seen from our low boat that seemed to play up almost from the rim of the horizon. I mention this because, as if the cows and calves had been purposely locked up in this innermost fold, and as if the wide extent of the herd had prevented them from learning the precise cause of its stopping — or possibly, being so young, unsophisticated, and in every way innocent and inexperienced — however it may have been, these smaller whales, now and then visiting our becalmed boat from the margin of the lake, showed a wondrous fearlessness and confidence, or else a spellbound panic that was impossible not to marvel at. Like household dogs, they came snuffling right up to our gunwales and touching them, until it almost seemed that some enchantment had suddenly domesticated them. Queequeg patted their foreheads. Starbuck scratched their backs with his lance, though, fearful of the consequences, he refrained from darting it for the time.

items.new: This terrific sight seemed to rouse the whole herd from their frozen fright. First, the whales forming the margin of our lake began to crowd a little and jostle against each other, as if lifted by half-spent waves from afar. Then the lake itself began faintly to heave and swell. The submarine nurseries and bridal chambers vanished. In tighter and tighter orbits, the whales in the more central circles began to swim in thickening clusters. Yes, the long calm was departing. A low advancing hum was soon heard. And then, like the tumultuous masses of block-ice when the great river Hudson breaks up in spring, the entire host of whales came tumbling upon their inner center, as if to pile themselves up in one common mountain. Instantly Starbuck and Queequeg changed places, Starbuck taking the stern.

items.new: When serenely traveling on one of these journeys, if any strange suspicious sights are seen, the lord whale keeps a wary eye on his interesting family. Should any rudely bold young Leviathan happen that way and presume to draw confidentially close to one of the ladies — with what prodigious fury the Bashaw (the pasha) assails him and chases him away! High times indeed, if unprincipled young rakes like him are to be permitted to invade the sanctity of domestic bliss. Though do what the Bashaw will, he cannot keep the most notorious Lothario out of his bed, for alas, all fish bed in common. As on shore, the ladies often cause the most terrible duels among their rival admirers. Just so with the whales, who sometimes come to deadly battle, and all for love. They fence with their long lower jaws, sometimes locking them together and striving for supremacy like elks that interlock their antlers in war. Not a few are captured bearing the deep scars of these encounters: furrowed heads, broken teeth, scalloped fins, and in some instances wrenched and dislocated mouths.

items.new: Mr. Erskine was counsel for the defendants; Lord Ellenborough was the judge. In the course of the defense, the witty Erskine went on to illustrate his position by alluding to a recent crim. con. case (a suit for adultery), in which a gentleman, after in vain trying to bridle his wife's viciousness, had at last abandoned her upon the seas of life. But in the course of years, repenting of that step, he brought an action to recover possession of her. Erskine had been on the other side, and he had then argued his position by saying that though the gentleman had originally harpooned the lady, and had once had her fast, and only by reason of the great stress of her plunging viciousness had at last abandoned her — yet abandon her he did, so that she became a Loose-Fish. And therefore when a subsequent gentleman re-harpooned her, the lady then became that subsequent gentleman's property, along with whatever harpoon might have been found sticking in her.

items.new: These arguments and counter-arguments being duly heard, the very learned judge officially decided as follows: As for the boat, he awarded it to the plaintiffs, because they had merely abandoned it to save their lives. But with regard to the disputed whale, harpoons, and line, they belonged to the defendants — the whale because it was a Loose-Fish at the time of the final capture, and the harpoons and line because when the fish made off with them, it (the fish) acquired property in those articles, and hence anybody who afterward took the fish had a right to them. Now the defendants afterward took the fish; therefore, the aforesaid articles were theirs.

items.new: Is it not a saying on everyone's lips that possession is half the law — regardless of how the thing came into possession? But often possession is the whole of the law. What are the bodies and souls of Russian serfs and Republican slaves but Fast-Fish, of which possession is the whole of the law? What to the greedy landlord is the widow's last mite but a Fast-Fish? What is yonder undetected villain's marble mansion with a door-plate for a waif — what is that but a Fast-Fish? What is the ruinous discount that Mordecai the broker gets from poor Woebegone the bankrupt, on a loan to keep Woebegone's family from starving — what is that ruinous discount but a Fast-Fish? What is the Archbishop of Savesoul's income of £100,000, seized from the meager bread and cheese of hundreds of thousands of broken-backed laborers, all sure of heaven without any of Savesoul's help — what is that globular £100,000 but a Fast-Fish? What are the Duke of Dunder's hereditary towns and hamlets but Fast-Fish? What to that mighty harpooner John Bull is poor Ireland but a Fast-Fish? What to that apostolic lancer Brother Jonathan is Texas but a Fast-Fish? And concerning all these, is not Possession the whole of the law?

Upon this, the poor sailors in their respectful consternation — so truly English — knowing not what to say, fell to vigorously scratching their heads all round, meanwhile ruefully glancing from the whale to the stranger. items.new: In his treatise on "Queen-Gold," or Queen's pin-money, an old King's Bench author, one William Prynne, writes thus: "The tail is the Queen's, that the Queen's wardrobe may be supplied with whalebone." Now this was written at a time when the black limber bone of the Greenland or right whale was widely used in ladies' bodices. But this same bone is not in the tail; it is in the head — which is a sad mistake for a learned lawyer like Prynne. But is the Queen a mermaid, to be presented with a tail? An allegorical meaning may lurk here.

items.new: Presently a breeze sprang up. Stubb pretended to cast off from the whale. Hoisting his boats, the Frenchman soon increased his distance, while the Pequod slid in between him and Stubb's whale. Whereupon Stubb quickly pulled to the floating body, and hailing the Pequod to give notice of his intentions, at once proceeded to reap the fruit of his unrighteous cunning. Seizing his sharp boat-spade, he commenced an excavation in the body, a little behind the side fin. You would almost have thought he was digging a cellar there in the sea. And when at length his spade struck against the gaunt ribs, it was like turning up old Roman tiles and pottery buried in fat English loam. His boat's crew were all in high excitement, eagerly helping their chief and looking as anxious as gold-hunters.

As a general thing, these ship-keepers are as hardy as the men in the boats' crews. But if there happens to be an unduly slender, clumsy, or timid fellow on the ship, that fellow is certain to be made a ship-keeper. It was so on the Pequod with the little negro nicknamed Pippin — Pip, for short. Poor Pip! You have heard of him before. You must remember his tambourine on that dramatic midnight, so gloomy-jolly.

items.new: In outward appearance, Pip and Dough-Boy made a matched pair, like a black pony and a white one of equal size though different color, driven together as one eccentric pair. But while hapless Dough-Boy was by nature dull and sluggish in his wits, Pip, though over tender-hearted, was at bottom very bright, with that pleasant, warm, jolly brightness peculiar to his tribe — a tribe who ever enjoy all holidays and festivities with finer, freer relish than any other race. For blacks, the year's calendar should show nothing but three hundred and sixty-five Fourth of Julys and New Year's Days. Nor smile while I write that this little black boy was brilliant, for even blackness has its brilliance: behold that lustrous ebony, paneled in kings' cabinets. But Pip loved life and all life's peaceful securities, so that the panic-striking business in which he had somehow become entangled had most sadly dimmed his brightness — though, as will soon be seen, what was thus temporarily subdued in him was destined in the end to be luridly illuminated by strange wild fires, that falsely showed him off to ten times the natural luster with which, in his native Tolland County in Connecticut, he had once enlivened many a fiddler's dance on the green and, at melodious twilight, with his gay ha-ha! had turned the round horizon into one star-belled tambourine. So, though in the clear light of day a pure diamond drop suspended against a blue-veined neck will glow with healthy beauty, yet when the cunning jeweler would show you the diamond in its most impressive luster, he lays it against a gloomy background and then lights it up not by the sun but by some unnatural gas. Then come those fiery blazes, infernally superb. Then the evil-blazing diamond, once the divinest symbol of the crystal skies, looks like some crown-jewel stolen from the King of Hell. But let us get to the story.

items.new: But we are all in the hands of the Gods, and Pip jumped again. It was under very similar circumstances to the first time, but now he did not carry the line overboard with him. And so when the whale started to run, Pip was left behind on the sea, like a hurried traveler's trunk. Alas! Stubb was but too true to his word. It was a beautiful, bountiful, blue day. The spangled sea was calm and cool, stretching flatly away on all sides to the horizon, like gold-beater's skin hammered out to the extreme. Bobbing up and down in that sea, Pip's ebony head showed like a head of cloves. No boat-knife was lifted when he fell so rapidly astern. Stubb's inexorable back was turned upon him, and the whale was winged. In three minutes, a whole mile of shoreless ocean lay between Pip and Stubb. Out from the center of the sea, poor Pip turned his crisp, curling, black head to the sun — another lonely castaway, though the loftiest and the brightest.
